Subject: NovaCorp post-demo: integration sysflow questions & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side so we can scope the POC and knock out the architecture questions your team raised.

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: Replace current edge reranker with an embeddings + on-device rerank flow, low-latency (<=250ms median per query) for top-5 suggestions.
- Traffic profile: ~1200 qps at peak across product catalog; median request payload ~300 tokens (user prompt + context).
- Compliance: audit logs and 13-month retention for query metadata, customer-managed keys preferred.

Architectural topics to resolve (short list)
1) SDK setup & auth: we support Node/Python/Go SDKs. For POC we recommend API key + IP allowlist for initial tests, then move to mTLS or OIDC for Dedicated/Private. We’ll include sample code in the runbook.
2) Routing & variants: runtime can route by policy (latency-first or cost-first). For your catalog we recommend routing 95% to the quantized 8-bit variant and 5% to full precision for quality checks.
3) Structured output & tool-calls: function/tool calling is supported — we can annotate outputs with JSON schema for safe parsing. If you need strict schema validation we’ll enable schema-mode that rejects invalid tool calls.
4) Embeddings + reranker: suggest using 1536-d embeddings with an in-memory ANN for root-candidate generation, then call a small reranker model (chat-style) for final scoring to keep latency bounds.
5) Request/response schema questions: chat vs completions — chat provides turn state and streaming tokens with function-calls; completions is simpler for single-shot prompts. Important differences below.

Important behavior notes (tokenization, streaming, limits)
- max_tokens: in chat, max_tokens is applied to the model response token budget for the completion portion; total token bill includes prompt + response. Be conservative with max_tokens for streaming tests — streaming sends tokens as they generate but still enforces max_tokens server-side.
- stop sequences: stop tokens are honored as soon as generated; with streaming the stream will terminate once stop is emitted but clients must still handle final metadata delta containing finish_reason.
- tokenization edgecases: embeddings use the same tokenizer as generation models; mismatched tokenizers between client-side length estimates and runtime can cause off-by-one. We recommend using our SDK token_count helper (included).

Next steps (proposed)
- I attached a compact POC runbook (redwood-poc-runbook-v1.pdf) and a small sample repo (poc-sample-code.zip) that shows Node + Python SDK bootstrap, API-key -> mTLS transition notes, and a minimal embedding+rerank pipeline.
- Technical deep dive: schedule 60-min session next week with your infra and security folks to confirm mTLS/KMS requirements.
- Acceptance criteria: <=250ms median, top-5 recall >= 92% vs current system on the seed dataset, no PII in logs.

Owners:
- Redwood: priyom (SE owner), ben (infra lead)
- NovaCorp: Alex (PM), Samantha (Infra)

Please confirm the deep-dive times that work for your team and any immediate priorities you want us to address in the runbook.

Thanks Priyom — solid recap. A few clarifying questions from our side before we loop infra/security: 

1) max_tokens semantics: if we set max_tokens=64 on a chat request that includes a 400-token prompt, does Redwood cap the response to 64 tokens but bill for 464 total tokens? And are there any internal truncation behaviors we should know about for long contexts?

2) Stop sequences + streaming: you mentioned the stream terminates when stop is emitted — in that case can we rely on receiving a final JSON delta containing finish_reason and token usage once the stream ends, or are there cases where streaming ends with no finish_reason? We need to know for our aggregator (we build final documents from streamed chunks).

3) Embeddings + reranker tokenization: if we pass the same prompt text to the embedding encoder and to the reranker model, will tokenization be identical (same splitter), or could there be differences across model types that would affect scoring/comparison?

4) SDK samples: can you confirm the SDK in the runbook includes an example for continuous streaming with reconnection semantics (client reconnect after transient network blip) and a small snippet showing backpressure/batching config?

5) For the routing policy: what happens if the quantized variant becomes unavailable mid-traffic — is there an automatic fallback to full-precision, and can that be set to fail-closed instead of fail-open? We want predictable cost spikes but no silent quality drops.

If you can address these 5 items in a short reply we can share with Samantha and Tim and pick a time for the technical deep dive.

—Alex

Alex — thanks for the focused list. Answers below (short) plus links to the exact code snippets in the attached repo/runbook. Happy to expand on any item in the deep-dive.

1) max_tokens & billing: correct — max_tokens limits the model output; billing is sum(prompt_tokens + response_tokens). If you set max_tokens=64 and prompt is 400 tokens, we will bill for prompt + actual response (<=64). For long contexts we support two behaviors: prefix-truncate (drop oldest tokens) or semantic-trim (we can provide a heuristic that trims low-salience parts of the context). The default is prefix-truncate; runbook shows how to enable semantic-trim for better quality.

2) stop sequences + streaming finish_reason: streaming will always emit a final metadata event with finish_reason when the model explicitly emits a stop or reaches max_tokens. Transient disconnects may cause the stream to close without a finish_reason; our SDK includes a resume-token mechanism so the client can reconnect and request missing deltas. See poc-sample-code.zip -> streaming/reconnect.md for the snippet.

3) tokenizer parity: embeddings and generation models on the same model family use the same tokenizer; however, if you run embeddings on a different model (e.g., text-embedding-3-small) and reranker on a chat model, tokenization can differ. Best practice: use the same tokenizer/model family for candidates used in reranking, or normalize by running our token_count helper before comparing lengths.

4) SDK streaming + reconnection: yes — the Node + Python samples include a small reconnect loop and an exponential backoff. The SDK exposes an onDelta callback and a resume_token you can persist. Backpressure: we expose a client-side batcher config (max_batch_tokens, max_batch_latency_ms); recommended starting point for your profile: max_batch_tokens=4096, max_batch_latency_ms=25.

5) routing failover semantics: by default the routing policy will failover to any compatible variant (we call this fail-open) to keep requests served. You can set the policy to fail-closed to return a 503 if the preferred variant is unavailable. For NovaCorp's latency/quality goals we recommend: prefer-quantized with automatic fallback to full-precision and a circuit-breaker that forces fail-closed if fallbacks exceed 10% of capacity in a 1-minute window. That prevents sustained cost spikes.

Next actions I can take today:
- Share a shorter one-page decision matrix (quantized vs fp32 behavior + recommended circuit breaker knobs).
- Schedule the 60-min deep dive with Ben (infra) and Laura (product infra) next Tue/Wed.

If that looks good I’ll drop the decision matrix and proposed calendar slots.

Thanks,
